title: Hypothesis (DNS) later ruled out; confirmed cause (expired cert)
notes: Tests hypothesis-vs-confirmed preservation: DNS is floated as a first guess and explicitly ruled out; the certificate expiry is the LOGS-CONFIRMED cause. An extractor must not harden the DNS guess into a fact, and must capture the confirmed cause distinctly.

turns.text: Prod is throwing intermittent TLS handshake failures. My first guess is it might be a DNS resolution flake — we've seen that before.
Could be. Let's check the cert too just in case.
Ok I just checked — logs confirm the cert actually expired 2 hours ago. That's the real cause, not DNS.
Got it, so DNS was just a hypothesis and turned out to be a red herring — confirmed root cause is the expired cert.

gold_atoms.text: TLS handshake failures were hypothesized to be a DNS resolution flake at first, but logs confirmed the actual cause was an expired certificate, not DNS.
The certificate had expired about 2 hours before the incident was investigated (confirmed via logs).

forbidden_items: DNS resolution was confirmed as the cause of the TLS failures
The cause was confirmed to be DNS
